subject: SIG: Identity guardrails — evidence packet and onboarding plan
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@greenbyte.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@greenbyte.com, sara.liu@greenbyte.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG - identity controls scope and evidence needs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. Greenbyte is running a SIG review for our vendor risk program and we'd like to close half of the identity controls section this week if possible (SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, MFA, least privilege). Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide for each area and a short timeline?

High level asks:
- Completed SIG identity questions (PDF or spreadsheet)
- Sample SCIM provisioning logs showing user create/update/deprovision events
- RBAC role inventory and mapping to least-privilege controls
- SAML metadata + proof of MFA enforcement for console/API access
- Short explanation of exception/temporary-access process

We prefer a single ZIP or Drive folder and a short mutual action plan (dates + owners). Our review kickoff is Thursday (11/05) so if you can share at least draft answers and evidence by EOD Wednesday that would be ideal.

Let me know if you need clarification.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis\Head of Vendor Risk\Greenbyte Inc.
(t.ellis@greenbyte.com)

PS: attaching our SIG spreadsheet template in case useful.
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@greenbyte.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - identity controls scope and evidence needs

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear asks. I'll own this on Redwood's side. Quick plan below and we can adjust based on your timeline: 

Proposed mutual action plan (high level)
- Wed, 11/04 EOD (today): Draft SIG responses + primary evidence (PDF + links) — owners: Marissa (evidence), Jordan (RBAC)
- Thu, 11/05: Q/A call if Greenbyte has clarifying questions (30 min)
- Fri, 11/06: Finalized packet uploaded to shared Drive and confirm receipt

What we'll provide (draft by EOD today):
- Completed SIG identity section (PDF) with inline references to evidence
- SCIM: redacted sample provisioning logs (user create/update/deprovision) and the provisioning flow diagram
- RBAC: role inventory CSV and summary of how roles map to least-privilege principles
- SAML/SSO: metadata file + note about IdP federation and MFA enforcement (we enforce MFA via conditional access for console + API tokens)
- Exception process: our temporary access policy + ticketing links and an audit example

Notes / quick clarifications needed from you: 
1) For SCIM proof, do you need raw logs with timestamps or redacted examples that show the sequence of events?
2) Any additional format preferences for the RBAC mapping (CSV vs spreadsheet with examples)?

Attachments referenced will be uploaded to the Drive link below; I'll follow up once Marissa attaches the files.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad\Security & Compliance Lead\Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@greenbyte.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - identity controls scope and evidence needs (attachments)

Hi team — attaching draft materials and evidence as discussed. See brief notes below for context.

-- Attachments (uploaded to Drive, also attached here): 
- redwood-sig-identity-answers-20261104.pdf (draft answers with references)
- rbac-role-inventory-20261104.csv (inventory of roles, privileges, owners)
- scim-provisioning-sample-logs-20261104.txt (redacted logs: shows create/update/deprovision events with timestamps; IDs masked)
- saml-metadata-redwood.xml (SP metadata, certificate fingerprints redacted)

Context / highlights:
- SCIM provisioning: We operate a SCIM-based provisioning pipeline for enterprise customers. The attached logs are redacted; raw logs are retained for 12 months and can be provided under a restricted access review if required.
- RBAC: The CSV maps each role to least-privilege rationale and lists role owners. We segregate admin privileges to a small group (4 individuals) and require ticketed approval for elevation; approvals are logged in Jira (link in Drive).
- MFA enforcement: MFA is enforced for interactive console access and refresh-token rotation is enforced for long-lived API clients. Evidence of recent MFA enforcement checks is cited in the PDF (page 3).
- Exception handling: Temporary access follows the "Just-in-time" process via our internal IAM workflow; exceptions require an approval ticket and are time-boxed. A recent example ticket (redacted) is linked in Drive.

Open items we will finalize after your quick review:
- Whether you want raw SCIM logs vs redacted samples (Marissa: we recommend redacted by default)
- Any additional detail on role-level permission justifications

If this looks good I'll add a short one-page diagram for the provisioning flow and upload it to the same folder.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole\Manager, Compliance Operations\Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(attachments: 4)
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@greenbyte.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@greenbyte.com>, compliance@greenbyte.com
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2026 17:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - identity controls scope and evidence needs

Mina / Marissa — received, thank you for the quick turnaround. The draft packet looks comprehensive. A couple quick follow-ups before our Thursday call: 

1) RBAC exceptions: can you add a one-paragraph summary of the approval SLAs and a redacted example of an elevation ticket (we saw the Drive link but would like a one-line summary in the packet)?
2) Provisioning diagram: yes please — the one-page flow will help our reviewers. If you can drop it in the folder by EOD Monday, that works.

Also would you be available for a 30-minute sync on Thu 11/05 at 10:00 AM PT? We want to walk through a couple of questions live. If that time doesn't work, propose an alternative.

Thanks again — appreciate the clear notes.

Tom Ellis\Head of Vendor Risk\Greenbyte Inc.
t.ellis@greenbyte.com
